newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa to pick up frequent flyer tax bill.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa to pick up frequent flyer tax bill.

text.p: Deutsche Lufthansa AG said it will in future pick up the tax bill for German taxpayers who cash in their frequent flyer miles and gain a financial benefit.
The airline said members of its Miles & More programme will continue to be able to use their miles tax-free under the 1997 German tax law now approved by the German parliament.
An annual personal tax-free allowance of 2,400 marks will be introduced and Lufthansa will pay tax liable above this sum at the rate of two percent, a spokeswoman told Reuters.
But she declined to say how much Lufthansa pays out in Miles & More benefits or how much tax it will have to pay to Bonn.
"The total sum of miles cashed in will be calculated to an average sum and that will be taxed at two percent," she said.
Lufthansa would also pay all tax owing on Miles & More benefits back-dated to January 1, 1993, to remove all financial uncertainties, a company statement said.
The spokeswoman said the demand of large German companies at a recent meeting to benefit from the programme through a points pool for firms was nothing new.
"The demand from companies that miles earned on company business should be used for the company is not a new subject," she said.
But Miles & More was an individual bonus scheme and companies benefited separately from corporate refunds on Lufthansa turnover, she pointed out.
"It is not planned to change the Miles & More concept," she stressed.
The Lufthansa Miles & More scheme has 2.1 million members, two-thirds of whom are registered in Germany. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44-171-542-7706 Fax+44-171-542-5017
